extracted.intended_audience: federal agency standards managers and technical standards program staff (DoD, DOE, FERC, NCS, etc.) responsible for implementing OMB Circular A-119 and related standards policy
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and reporting requirements for federal agencies on use, adoption, conversion, and participation in voluntary consensus standards under OMB Circular A-119 and P.L. 104-113, including agency policies, processes, and metrics to report. Targets implementation practices (DoD, DOE, FERC, NCS) and standards-development participation rules (e.g., GISB).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt voluntary consensus standards where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should use voluntary consensus standards in preference to government-unique standards when the voluntary standard is acceptable to meet agency requirements and when items/materials are normally procured using a voluntary standard by commercial firms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DoD and DOE policies state a preference to adopt National Consensus and other commercial/industry standards; DoD 4120.3-M requires standards developers to actively look for opportunities to replace government documents with voluntary standards. The Department relies on military specifications in lieu of voluntary standards only when justified as truly military-unique, when no voluntary standard exists and development is not imminent, or when there is no industry interest to develop a voluntary standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: DoD requirement to seek replacement of military documents
rubrics_metrics.description: DoD standards developers are required to actively look for opportunities to replace government documents with voluntary standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implemented through DoD 4120.3-M 'Defense Standardization Program Policies and Procedures'; part of the MilSpec Reform initiative which reviewed 30,000+ military specifications to identify candidates for conversion and put procedures in place to prevent proliferation of military documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justified exceptions for using military-unique standards
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may rely on military specifications/standards rather than voluntary standards only when the requirement can be justified as truly military-unique; when a voluntary standard does not exist and development is not imminent; or when there is no industry interest to develop a voluntary standard to address agency requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DoD explicitly lists these as the conditions under which it will continue to rely on military specifications and standards in lieu of voluntary standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for national consensus standards in DOE directives
rubrics_metrics.description: DOE directives (e.g., DOE P251.1) establish a preference to adopt National Consensus Standards and other commercial and industry standards as the foundation of the Department's directives system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOE restricts use of mandated technical standards in rulemaking and Orders, references appropriate voluntary consensus standards when acceptable, and uses performance-based rules (e.g., DOE P410.1A) that permit adoption of commercial/industry standards as acceptable methods to implement the rules when appropriate for the work and hazards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the 'Work Smart' necessary-and-sufficient standards process
rubrics_metrics.description: DOE contractors, with DOE approval, may identify and apply a 'necessary and sufficient' set of standards (including voluntary consensus standards) that best fit their activities, focusing on outcomes and performance rather than prescriptive methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referred to as the 'Work Smart' approach; supported by DOE P450.3 and DOE M450.3-1; field pilot projects demonstrated efficiencies and cost-savings; the approach was expanded to cover a broad range of programs and facilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: TSPO responsibilities and five-year standards review cycle
rubrics_metrics.description: The DOE Technical Standards Program Office (TSPO) must identify voluntary standards suitable for DOE needs, support conversion of Department standards to voluntary standards, develop/maintain databases, meet reporting requirements, and coordinate day-to-day technical standards activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TSPO procedures establish a five-year standards review cycle to check for continued applicability and provide guidance on conversion of Department standards to voluntary standards; TSPO also develops procedures, methods, and training approaches to implement the program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish topical standards committees composed of subject-matter experts
rubrics_metrics.description: DOE should recognize topical standards committees composed of subject matter experts to serve as focal points for standards activities in specific technical areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Topical committees provide a forum for interested DOE parties to review voluntary standards, address application issues, and develop Department and Federal positions on standards issues; DOE recognized 19 topical committees as of October 1998.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report number of voluntary consensus standards bodies and agency participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must report the number of voluntary consensus standards bodies in which the agency participates and the number of agency employees participating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example DOE reporting: Number of standards bodies: 65; Number of agency personnel participating: 681; Total number of agency participation: 1321. This is a required metric under the reporting provisions of OMB Circular A-119 / P.L. 104-113.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report number of voluntary consensus standards used
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must report the number of voluntary consensus standards the agency has used since the specified date based on the procedures set forth in the Circular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example DOE reported 840 voluntary standards used since October 1, 1997. Reporting should follow sections 11 and 12 of the Circular.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify voluntary standards substituted for government-unique standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must identify voluntary consensus standards that have been substituted for government-unique standards as a result of agency review under the Circular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOE response example: identification of substituted standards: 0 (no substitutions recorded in FY 1998). Agencies should document substitutions (or lack thereof) as part of their report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate effectiveness of standards policy and recommend changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must provide an evaluation of the effectiveness of their policy on voluntary standards use and recommend any changes to that policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOE's evaluation stated that OMB Circular A-119 guidance appears sufficient, allows latitude for agency-tailored approaches, and places emphasis on outcomes rather than processes. Agencies should use their evaluation to recommend revisions if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report instances of using government-unique standards in lieu of voluntary standards
rubrics_metrics.description: As required by P.L. 104-113, agencies must report when they used a government-unique standard instead of an equivalent existing voluntary consensus standard, and explain why.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOE reported no recorded cases in FY 1998. Agencies must document any such cases and the justification under the exceptions listed in policy (e.g., truly military-unique).

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporate voluntary standards by reference in regulations (FERC practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may incorporate voluntary consensus standards by reference into its regulations rather than participating directly in standards bodies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERC typically incorporates standards by reference; with GISB it gave great weight to consensus proposals and adopted GISB standards (e.g., Order Nos. 587 series and 587-H) to standardize business practices and electronic communications across the industry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage industry-led consensus standards development (GISB example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies can encourage industry to develop voluntary standards through consensus organizations (e.g., GISB) and rely on those consensus processes for standards to be implemented across an industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERC convened technical conferences, encouraged formation of industry working groups, and anticipated GISB would be the forum to coordinate industry efforts; standards developed by GISB were accepted and incorporated by FERC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards organization governance and consensus thresholds (GISB rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards developed by a consensus organization should follow balanced representation and explicit approval thresholds to ensure genuine industry consensus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GISB governance examples: balanced voting representation from five industry segments; prospective standards require at least 17 affirmative votes in the Executive Committee with at least two affirmative votes from each segment; membership ratification requires 67% affirmative of ballots; Board of Directors changes need 19 affirmative votes with at least two from each segment. GISB has filed with ANSI for accreditation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency engagement with voluntary standards organizations and international bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should work extensively with voluntary standards organizations, international bodies, and participate in relevant committees to ensure government requirements are considered during standards development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: OMNCS/FTSC participates in ANSI-accredited organizations, international groups (ITU-T, ITU-R, ISO, IEC), and many industry forums; DOE participates on ANSI boards and international ISO technical committees. Agencies should document participation and liaison roles.
